articles.title: Texas football: Rivalry win over Aggies sends Longhorns to SEC Championship Game
articles.summary: On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win at Texas A&M. With the victory, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game in Atlanta.
body: COLLEGE STATION – After surviving an evening on Texas A&M's campus, the Texas football team is heading to Atlanta.

On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win over Texas A&M at Kyle Field. With its fourth straight win in this in-state rivaly, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game at Atlanta's Mercedes-Benz Stadium.

The Longhorns got some offense in Friday's victory as Cam Coleman hauled in a touchdown and Gianni Spetic kicked three field goals. But any postgame game balls belonged to a defense that held Texas A&M to 234 yards of offense while recording two sacks and forcing one turnover and two turnover on downs.
Texas A&M (4-8) finishes its third season under head coach Mike Elko with its fewest wins since 2008. The Aggies were just 1-8 in SEC play.
points: On Friday, No. 3 Texas had its defense lead the way to a 16-6 win at Texas A&M.
With the victory, Texas (10-2, 7-2) advances to play Georgia in next weekend's SEC Championship Game in Atlanta.

articles.title: What went wrong for Alonso's Chelsea at Forest?
articles.summary: Xabi Alonso called for his Chelsea side to get back to the fundamentals before kick-off - and then watched on as they were outworked and outclassed on their way to a miserable 3-2 defeat at Nottingham Forest.
body: "Everyone in the club and team, we need to stick together and go through this moment. We have to deal with it and we are responsible," Alonso told Sky Sports after the game, which marked their third successive defeat in the Premier League.
"It is a difficult moment for everyone at the club. For the team and the fans. Disappointed to lose again but we need to keep trying to find solutions.
"We can't stop. We are low in confidence. At this level you need to hold results and not concede so much. That is why we are losing."

Alonso now has as many losses in 15 games across all competitions as he did in 34 for Real Madrid (6). Since March, no side has more defeats in the top-flight than the Blues (14). And their problems are mounting by the day.

articles.title: George MacIntyre set to start at QB for Tennesvs. Vanderbilt
articles.summary: Vanderbilt appeared first on ClutchPoints. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here. Tennessee football is preparing for another quarterback change ahead of its regular-season finale against Vanderbilt.
body: There were questions surrounding Tennessee’s quarterback situation moving forward, particularly after the Volunteers used both MacIntyre and Faizon Brandon during their 27-13 victory over LSU. However, according to On3 insiders Chris Low and Pete Nakos, the coaching staff has decided to give MacIntyre the starting opportunity against Vanderbilt.

“George MacIntyre is set to start at quarterback for Tennessee against Vanderbilt, On3’s Chris Low and Pete Nakos reported. Faizon Brandon is also expected to see play during the Week 13 matchup on Saturday,” Nick Schultz of On3 wrote.

MacIntyre was still working his way back from an injury when Brandon received the opportunity to start against LSU. However, Tennessee eventually brought both quarterbacks into the game and ultimately won it. The win improved Tennessee’s overall record to 9-2 and its SEC record to 6-2.
MacIntyre initially suffered the injury during the Volunteers’ Week 11 victory over Texas A&M. His absence forced the coaching staff to turn to Brandon for the starting responsibilities against LSU.

articles.title: No Rodgers, no problem! Steelers shock Broncos after dramatic week
articles.summary: It had been a week clouded by Aaron Rodgers and his explosive claims regarding head coach Mike McCarthy, but the Pittsburgh Steelers swatted at the storm to claim a shock 27-5 win over the Super Bowl-contending Denver Broncos on Black Friday.
body: Broncos quarterback Bo Nix endured a miserable afternoon as he surrendered two interceptions and a lost fumble that resulted in two defensive touchdowns for the Steelers.

Denver trailed 24-5 after a dire first half in which they were limited to just 58 yards of offense, becoming just the third team since 1991 to post fewer than 60 yards while conceding two defensive touchdowns over the first two quarters of a game.

TJ Watt scored with an end zone fumble recovery, Jalen Ramsey returned a Nix interception to the house and D.K. Metcalf recorded a touchdown catch before appearing to celebrate by holding up eight fingers in an apparent support of Rodgers.
The Broncos looked anything but a contender as they slumped to 8-3, while the Steelers distanced themselves from a reflection of turmoil to improve to 7-4 in their push for the playoffs.

articles.title: Price out in Players Championship Finals first round in night of upsets
articles.summary: Three of darts' biggest names were subject to shock upsets in the Players Championship Finals as Grand Slam champion Gerwyn Price, World No 2 Gian Van Veen, and No 1 seed Wessel Nijman were all knocked out in the first round at Minehead.
body: Price was beaten by 6-4 Sebastian Bialecki - the first time the Pole had beaten the Welshman in his career - while Jeffery de Graaf won two legs on the bounce to consign van Veen to defeat by the same scoreline.
Nijman was upset by 20-year-old Henry Coates despite posting an average of 110 - the second-highest average in Players Championship Finals history.

World No 4 Luke Humphries, meanwhile, battled through his recurring back injury to secure a routine 6-3 victory against Darryl Pilgrim, while Michael van Gerwen withstood Connor Scutt to secure safe passage with a 6-3 first-round win of his own.

Beau Greaves also progressed to the second round with a scrappy 6-3 victory against former Lakeside champion Christian Kist despite a mediocre average of 89.64, and will face Rob Owen in the next round.

articles.title: 'You're not welcome here' - Chelsea fans turn on Fofana
articles.summary: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana is booed by his own fans during the Premier League defeat at Nottingham Forest after a controversial interview.
body: Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana was subjected to repeated boos and told "you're not welcome here" by his own fans during Friday's Premier League defeat by Nottingham Forest.
The jeers aimed at the 25-year-old were heard every time he touched the ball and came after an unauthorised interview with French YouTuber Zach Nani was released.
In that controversial two-hour conversation, Fofana also appeared to joke about missing his penalty during last month's Carabao Cup shootout defeat by Liverpool.
Manager Xabi Alonso said the French centre-back had apologised and "it won't be repeated".

articles.title: Baylor set to hire UTSA coach Jeff Traylor after leading Roadrunners to new heights
articles.summary: The former Texas high school coaching legend, who went 61-28 with three 10-win seasons at UTSA, takes over in Waco after Dave Aranda was fired in October
body: Baylor is set to hire UTSA coach Jeff Traylor to the same position, according to CBS Sports' Matt Zenitz. The former Texas high school coach clinched a spot in the American Conference title game on Friday.

Traylor is a legendary Texas high school football coach at Gilmer High School in East Texas, winning three state championships and earning a spot in the THSCA Hall of Honor. After stints as an assistant at Texas, SMU and Arkansas, he was named head coach at UTSA in 2020, where he helped lead the Roadrunners to an unprecedented stretch of success.

The Roadrunners went 61-28 under Traylor's watch, including three 10-win seasons. They're playing for their third conference title in six years, and first since transitioning to the American in 2023. UTSA began playing football in 2011 and had never previously recorded more than 7 wins as an FBS program.
